title: Espaces stratifiés et voisinages côniques (ou : déploiement des espaces stratifiés) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 15-18): X is a topological space, Y ⊂ X a closed subspace (a stratum or union of strata), and T a conic neighbourhood of Y. That is, T is the mapping cylinder of a map Ṫ → Y, with Ṫ the 'boundary' of T, and λT for λ ∈ ]0,1[ the shrunken neighbourhoods. On the previous page he defined a cylindrical neighbourhood E ≅ B×[0,1] of a closed subset B. He also defined when a closed subset X' is 'compatible' (later renamed 'transversal') with E: X'∩E = B'×[0,1] with B' = X'∩B.

This page:

(3) Compatibility of a part with a family. A part B of X is compatible with a family (X_i) of parts of X if there is a cylindrical (or semi-cylindrical) neighbourhood of B that is compatible with every X_i. The margin hesitates over the terminology (compatible vs. transversal).

Remark: strict compatibility. Let T be a strict conic neighbourhood of Y. T is strictly compatible with a family X_i ⊂ X if two conditions hold:
- T is compatible with each X_i, i.e. X_i ∩ T = T·(X_i ∩ Ṫ). Each X_i meets T in the sub-cone (mapping cylinder) over its trace on Ṫ.
- Ṫ is a collared (cylindrically bordered) part of the complement X* = X ∖ T̊, compatible with the family X_i* = X* ∩ X_i.

Then X_i ∩ Ṫ is a well-collared boundary not only of X_i ∩ T but also of X_i*. The margin rewrites this as X_i ∩ Ṫ = ∂X_i*.

In modern terms: removing the open cone T̊ 'unfolds' X along Y. It produces a space X* with collared boundary Ṫ, and the strata X_i must be cut transversally, so that each X_i* is again a space with collared boundary. This is one step of the 'déploiement' (unzipping/blow-up) of a stratified space into a manifold-with-corners-like object.

(4) Equisingularity. A strict conic neighbourhood T of Y is called équisingulier (the machine transcription's 'quasi-régulier' is wrong) if the projection Ṫ → Y is a locally trivial fibration. T is équisingulier for a family of parts T_i ⊂ T if moreover:
- the T_i are conic;
- each Ṫ_i → Y is locally trivial;
- and even (next page) the pair (Ṫ, Ṫ_i) is locally trivial over Y.

The next page then defines: X with (X_i) is equisingular along Y if some conic neighbourhood is equisingular for the traces X_i ∩ T. It follows that each X_i ∩ Y is open and closed in Y. This is the topological analogue of Whitney/Thom-Mather local triviality along a stratum, i.e. a locally cone-like (CS / Siebenmann) structure with a locally trivial link bundle, adapted to a family of closed subsets.
errors: No mathematical error. The definitions are preliminary, and several conditions (strict vs. non-strict, cylindrical vs. semi-cylindrical) are left in flux, with crossed-out alternatives.
The parenthesis 'X_i ∩ T = T·X_i ∩ Ṫ' should be read as X_i ∩ T = T·(X_i ∩ Ṫ), the cone over the trace; read literally it is ambiguous.
Implicit gap: 'Ṫ is a sub-space of X*' must mean that Ṫ admits a (semi-)cylindrical collar in X* = X∖T̊. Without such a collar the notion ∂X_i* is not defined.

ideas.what: Compatibility (transversality) of a family of closed subsets with a cylindrical/collar neighbourhood of a closed set B
ideas.modern_name: Collars compatible with a stratification / stratified collar
ideas.usually_credited_to: Brown (collaring theorem, 1962); Siebenmann (1972) for stratified collars

ideas.what: Strict compatibility: complement X∖T̊ of an open conic neighbourhood has Ṫ as collared boundary, cut transversally by all strata (X_i ∩ Ṫ = ∂X_i*)
ideas.modern_name: Removing a regular/mapping-cylinder neighbourhood to get a stratified space with boundary; unzipping / blow-up along a stratum
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 sketches the 'déploiement' philosophy but not these definitions

ideas.what: Équisingularity of a conic neighbourhood: Ṫ → Y locally trivial, also for the sub-cones Ṫ_i (as a pair)
ideas.modern_name: Locally trivial link bundle / Thom–Mather local triviality along a stratum; CS-sets; conically stratified spaces
ideas.usually_credited_to: Whitney, Thom, Mather; Siebenmann (1972); Lurie (Higher Algebra, App. A)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §5 (general discussion of tubular neighbourhood theory for stratified spaces)

missed.claim: Grothendieck's 'strict compatibility' builds the complement X* = X∖T̊ with Ṫ as a collared boundary that all strata cut transversally. This is precisely the inductive step of the unzipping/déploiement later formalised by Ayala–Francis–Tanaka for conically smooth stratified spaces. Here it is done purely topologically and for an arbitrary family of closed subsets.
missed.quote: si Ṫ est une [partie bordante?] de X* = X ∖ T̊, compatible avec la famille des X_i* = X* ∩ X_i
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a topological (non-smooth) version of unzipping. Recent work on exit-path categories and topological stratified spaces lacks it in this generality; it is minor, but documents Grothendieck's priority of formulation.

deep.surprise_reason: The page consists of foundational definitions (compatible collars, strict conic neighbourhoods, equisingularity as local triviality of the link). These are close to Siebenmann/Mather/Quinn notions. The only noteworthy point is the explicit unfolding step anticipating later 'unzipping' constructions.
transcription_corrections: 'on dit quasi-régulier' should read 'on dit équisingulier' (underlined in the image).
'Il est dit régulier pour une famille' should read 'Il est dit équisingulier pour une famille'.
'si de plus les Y_i sont côniques' should read 'si de plus les T_i sont côniques'.
'dans ce cas on dit que X_i ∩ T est un sous-espace bien' is more likely 'X_i ∩ Ṫ est une partie bord(ante) bien [collée] (non seulement de X_i ∩ T, mais aussi) de X_i*'.
Margin near (3) seems to discuss whether to replace 'compatible' by the term 'transversalité', consistent with the previous page's renaming.
'voisinage cylindrique (ou semi cylindrique)' is plausible; the parenthetical is written above the line as an insertion.
